Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present second bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 74 of 2018,
S.T. No. 1042 of 2018 (Ashu Yadav Vs. State of U.P.), under Sections 376, 328, 506 I.P.C., Section 4/5 POCSO Act and Section 67 of I.T. Act, Police Station Anwarganj, District Kanpur Nagar, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

sentences.text: It has been argued by the learned counsel for applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

The alleged incident has been shown of 01.11.2017, whereas, F.I.R.
has been registered on 02.05.2018 and there is no satisfactory explanation for delay in lodging of FIR.
The victim girl has made false and baseless allegations of rape against the applicant.

It was pointed out that in alleged hotel, where she was subjected to alleged rape, no entry of applicant or of Ashu Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108603922/

sentences.text: victim girl has been found in Hotel register and thus, there is no evidence that victim girl was taken to said hotel.
The victim girl has refused to undergo internal medical examination and thus, the prosecution version regarding rape of victim is not supported by medical evidence.
Age of victim has been shown 17 years.
It is further submitted that that first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 28.02.2020 and after that all the material witnesses have already been examined.
Referring to the statements of the witnesses, it was submitted that there are material contradictions in the statements of witnesses.

It is further submitted that there are a number of formal witnesses, who are yet to be examined, and thus, trial of the case is likely to take sufficient long time in its conclusion, whereas, applicant is languishing in jail since 04.05.2018 and he has already undergone the custody of about five years.
It was submitted that in case applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail application.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Ashu Yadav, involved in aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
